# Walnut of Vendor Contracts (`walnut-of-vendor-contracts`)

Vendor contract analysis for nursing homes: auto-renewal notice dates coming up or passed, expired contracts still billing, spend with no contract, price increases above the contract escalator and charges above contracted rates. Vendor contact details are masked before results reach the model.

**Walnut never sends termination or renewal notices.**

Evergreen ver 1 · Financial services · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · resident and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`evergreen-core`](../evergreen-core)

```bash
npx -y walnut-of-vendor-contracts demo
npx -y walnut-of-vendor-contracts mcp --root ./facility-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional Cedar Hollow vendor contracts, reviewed on 1 April 2026. Planted:

- Lone Star Linen renews automatically on 30 June unless notice is given by 1 May, and its price per pound rose 16.67% against a 3% escalator.
- The Bluebonnet Food Service notice date passed on 2 March, so it renews on 31 May.
- The Prairie Medical Supply contract ended 31 December 2025, and it is still billing. Its brief price rose 3.28% against a 3% escalator.
- Hilltop Floor Care has 12800 of spend and no contract.
- Gulf Coast Pharmacy billed 22.00 against a 19.50 contract price.

Vendor emails and phone numbers are in [`phi-canaries.json`](fixtures/phi-canaries.json); they must never reach the model. [`rules-typo.json`](fixtures/rules-typo.json) misspells a setting, so the check refuses it.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `walnut_check` | Check vendor contracts against dates and spend. | runs |
| `walnut_write_report` | Write walnut-vendor-contracts.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and walnut-vendor-contracts.html into out_dir (default evergreen-out/walnut). | runs |
| `walnut_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `walnut_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `walnut_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `walnut_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `contract_notice_send` | Walnut never sends termination or renewal notices. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `walnut_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `contracts` (required) | Vendor contract list under --root: vendor, contract number, start, end, auto renew, notice days, escalator percent, contact |
| `spend` (required) | Vendor spend lines under --root: vendor, date, amount, item code, quantity, unit price |
| `prices` | Optional contract price list under --root: vendor, item code, rate |
| `rules` | Optional rules JSON: warn_days, no_contract_over |
| `as_of` | Review date (YYYY-MM-DD, default today) |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold resident or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx walnut-of-vendor-contracts inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Vendor contracts (`contracts`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `vendor` (required) | text | Vendor, Vendor Name, Supplier, Payee |
| `contract_no` | text | Contract, Contract #, Contract Number, Agreement |
| `start` | date | Start, Start Date, Effective Date |
| `end` | date | End, End Date, Expiration, Expires, Term End |
| `auto_renew` | text | Auto Renew, Evergreen, Renews, Automatic Renewal |
| `notice_days` | number | Notice Days, Notice Period, Termination Notice |
| `escalator_pct` | number | Escalator, Escalator %, Annual Increase, Price Increase Cap |
| `contact_email` | text (masked) | Contact Email, Email, Vendor Email |
| `contact_phone` | text (masked) | Contact Phone, Phone, Vendor Phone |

### Vendor spend (`spend`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `vendor` (required) | text | Vendor, Vendor Name, Supplier, Payee |
| `date` (required) | date | Date, Invoice Date, Posted |
| `amount` (required) | amount | Amount, Amt, Total, Balance, Net Amount, Payment Amount, Paid, Paid Amount |
| `code` | text | Code, Item, Item Code, SKU, Service Code |
| `qty` | number | Qty, Quantity, Units |
| `unit_price` | amount | Unit Price, Price, Rate, Each |

### Contract prices (`prices`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `vendor` (required) | text | Vendor, Vendor Name, Supplier, Payee |
| `code` (required) | text | Code, Item, Item Code, SKU, Service Code |
| `rate` (required) | amount | Rate, Contract Rate, Contract Price, Price |

## Settings file (`walnut_rules`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `warn_days` | Flag notice deadlines within this many days (default 60) |
| `no_contract_over` | Flag spend with no contract at or above this amount (default 10000) |

## Memory

`walnut_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `walnut_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `contract_note` | is shown with results. It never changes a check. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `evergreen-core` and `remedy-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "walnut-of-vendor-contracts": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "walnut-of-vendor-contracts",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/facility-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add walnut-of-vendor-contracts -- npx -y walnut-of-vendor-contracts mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
walnut-of-vendor-contracts tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
walnut-of-vendor-contracts sources               # the columns each input is read from
walnut-of-vendor-contracts inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
walnut-of-vendor-contracts call walnut_check '{"contracts":"<contracts>","spend":"<spend>"}'
walnut-of-vendor-contracts eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
walnut-of-vendor-contracts demo
```

## Resident and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: resident and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to PointClickCare, MatrixCare, a payer portal, a bank, a state Medicaid portal or a payroll system.
- Medicare, Medicaid and payroll rules are summarised from public material as of 2026 and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, payroll or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, tax, accounting, clinical, reimbursement or HIPAA advice. A person decides what to bill, pay, appeal, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
